assumptions: Stripe host is api.stripe.com and Plaid host is production.plaid.com, as they appear in the workspace
Customer's 'approved list' is exactly Stripe and Plaid; no other vendor is approved
Advisory enforcement is the right default for new policies; blocking is the owner's decision
Policy-only change is acceptable for 'build all of it': no object code changed, because removing raw card columns or the debug log changes product behaviour and stored data
Card-adjacent field list: card_number, card_cvv, card_expiry, cardholder_name, card_last4, bank_account_number, bank_routing_number
confusions: The skill's policies topic and the templates doc give slightly different 'Fill' guidance for LOG-001 and DATA-010 (object_kinds param present in catalogue but not in the doc summary); I took the catalogue JSON as authoritative
Skill says exceeding exit codes and policy evaluate are the honest checks, but evaluate is forbidden in this run; I could not confirm the findings I predicted
Unclear whether a forbidden-field rule should cover every field in the PCI list or only the ones the recipe names (card_number, cvv, cvc, pan); I used the customer's list
The skill says a policy file carries no comments, but there is no explicit statement whether tags on the policy itself are free-form or vocabulary-bound; I used pci-dss
wished_for: A PCI DSS recipe with fields for the card and bank field names and a worked example for bank account numbers, which the current recipe does not cover
A check or param for datadog.log in LOG-001, or a note in the template that it covers only debug.log
A way to rate whether a vendor host receives card data, rather than only whether it is on the list
Guidance on what to do when the policy would flag existing code that the customer is not ready to change (advisory vs blocking, finding triage)
why_confidence: The policies parse and the dry run accepts them, and they cover the customer's three stated rules at the level of stored definitions: card data is not logged via debug.log, not stored in declared fields, and vendor hosts are limited to Stripe and Plaid. Confidence is not high because the policies were not evaluated (evaluate was forbidden in this run), so predicted findings are unverified, and the policies cannot see runtime logging, vendor payloads, or the wider PCI controls. The raw card columns and charge logging remain in the code until the customer changes them.
